content: An iodate is a chemical compound that represents a salt derived from iodic acid. In the iodate anion, iodine is covalently bonded to three oxygen atoms, and its molecular formula is IO₃⁻. The molecular geometry of the iodate ion is trigonal pyramidal. Iodate can be synthesized by reducing periodate using a thioether as the reducing agent. The reaction produces a sulfoxide as a byproduct. Iodates belong to a class of chemical compounds that contain the iodate group. Examples of iodates include sodium iodate (NaIO₃), silver iodate (AgIO₃), and calcium iodate (Ca(IO₃)₂). Structurally, iodates are similar to chlorates, except that iodine replaces chlorine in the compound. Under acidic conditions, iodic acid is formed from iodates. Potassium hydrogen iodate (KH(IO₃)₂) is a double salt composed of potassium iodate and iodic acid, and it also functions as an acid. Iodates are commonly utilized in the iodine clock reaction, a well-known chemical reaction used to study reaction kinetics.
